title: 1920-1922 Rebuilding the bridge and replacing wood piers with concrete
description: The disaster of April 6, 1920, forced residents to rely once again on ferries, ice bridges, or long trips to Florenceville or Woodstock to cross the river. Frustrated, citizens called for a steel bridge, but the cost was prohibitive. Instead, the government launched a major project: replacing the wooden piers with concrete, rebuilding the two lost spans, and covering the entire bridge to improve its durability. Though people initially disliked the covered bridge, describing it as a long, dark tunnel and worrying about young couples lingering or unsavoury characters hiding inside, they ultimately accepted it out of necessity. After two years of construction, the bridge reopened in early 1922. Little did anyone realize how beloved this iconic covered bridge would become for future generations. (Photo courtesy of Vanessa Dickinson)
